e.title: **预注册的校准审计：十个死亡率预测族、七种不确定性机制，在疫情这道断点上**：仓库 `Hamid-Jahani/mortality-calibration-under-shift`——**`PREREGISTRATION.md` 在**第一次用真实数据拟合之前就已提交**，**并附** sha256**（**逐字** `bbbe3860a5446d063e186e56555afa893b07c36cf15a990d07567471affe50be`**）**；**⭐ 结论里有一条是**对己不利**的**（**逐字**「**The registered one-sided H2 is refuted.**」**）；**⭐ 而最实用的一条是**年金因子**那条****（**Lee–Carter 对 ä₆₅ 的名义 95% 区间在**平静期**只覆盖 **0.253****）**
e.title_en: A pre-registered calibration audit of ten mortality forecasting families and seven uncertainty mechanisms across a pandemic break, in a repository whose preregistration file was committed with a SHA-256 hash before the first model was fitted to real data, whose findings include one that refutes its own registered hypothesis, and whose most practical warning is that a nominal ninety-five percent interval for an annuity factor covered only about a quarter of realisations even in the quiet stable period.
e.title_hk: **預註冊的校準審計：十個死亡率預測族、七種不確定性機制，在疫情這道斷點上**：倉庫 `Hamid-Jahani/mortality-calibration-under-shift`——**`PREREGISTRATION.md` 在**第一次用真實資料擬合之前就已提交**，**並附** sha256**；**⭐ 結論裡有一條是**對己不利**的**（**逐字**「**The registered one-sided H2 is refuted.**」**）；**⭐ 而最實用的一條是**年金因子**那條****（**Lee–Carter 對 ä₆₅ 的名義 95% 區間在**平靜期**只覆蓋 **0.253****）**
e.summary: **mortality-calibration-audit**（`Hamid-Jahani/mortality-calibration-under-shift`，**逐字副标题**「**A Pre-Registered Calibration Audit of Ten Forecasting Families and Seven Uncertainty Mechanisms Across the COVID-19 Break**」）**是一份**可靠性审计**：**逐字自述**「**A reliability audit of probabilistic mortality forecasts across a structural break. The contribution is the audit and the reusable evaluation protocol — not a new architecture.**」**——**⭐ 即**它明说自己**不是提出新模型**，**而是**审计别人模型的不确定性**。**本次实测**：**创建 2026-08-25、最后推送 2026-09-08**、**★1**、**主语言 TeX**；**许可 MIT**（**`LICENSE` 逐字前两行为** MIT License／Copyright (c) 2026 Hamid Jahani**）**；**tarball 枚举 192 条路径**（**其中** `tests/` **23 个测试、**`docs/` 7 份、**`scripts/` 21 个、**`paper/` 含 12 张图的 PDF 与完整 LaTeX**）**。**本条目属于本轮主题**「下游：把上游当成尺子」**——**⭐ 它把已收录的 [[stmomo]] 当作**数值预言机**（**逐字**「**R/StMoMo oracle parity (β relative difference 2.4e-14)**」**）**，**数据用 [[human-mortality-db]]**。**⭐⭐⭐ 四处最值得抄**：**① **预注册带哈希、且写明早于第一次拟合****（**逐字给出 sha256 与「**before the first model was fitted to real data**」**，**并逐字说**「**every deviation since is recorded in the four addenda**」**）**；**② **一条注册假设被自己**否定****（**「**The registered one-sided H2 is refuted.**」**）**；**③ **七条方法学规则逐字被称为**「**binding, not aspirational**」**（**含**「**Never a random split — mortality panels leak trivially**」**）**；**④ **数据不可再分发被写明并给出自取路径 ＋ sha256 清单**。**⚠️ 本次未运行任何一步、**未读论文正文**。
e.summary_hk: **mortality-calibration-audit**（`Hamid-Jahani/mortality-calibration-under-shift`，**逐字副標題**「**A Pre-Registered Calibration Audit of Ten Forecasting Families and Seven Uncertainty Mechanisms Across the COVID-19 Break**」）**是一份**可靠性審計**：**逐字自述**「**The contribution is the audit and the reusable evaluation protocol — not a new architecture.**」**。**本次實測**：**建立 2026-08-25、最後推送 2026-09-08**、**★1**、**TeX**；**許可 MIT**；**tarball 列舉 192 條路徑**（**`tests/` 23 個、**`docs/` 7 份、**`scripts/` 21 個**）**。**本條目屬於本輪主題**「下游：把上游當尺子」**——**⭐ 它把已收錄的 [[stmomo]] 當**數值預言機**（**逐字**「**R/StMoMo oracle parity (β relative difference 2.4e-14)**」**）**，**資料用 [[human-mortality-db]]**。**⭐⭐⭐ 四處最值得抄**：**① **預註冊帶雜湊、且寫明早於第一次擬合**；**② **一條註冊假設被自己**否定**（**「**The registered one-sided H2 is refuted.**」**）**；**③ **七條方法學規則逐字被稱為**「**binding, not aspirational**」**；**④ **資料不可再分發被寫明並給出自取路徑＋sha256 清單**。**⚠️ 本次未運行任何一步、未讀論文正文**。
e.summary_en: The repository mortality-calibration-under-shift, subtitled as a pre-registered calibration audit of ten forecasting families and seven uncertainty mechanisms across a pandemic break, **is a reliability audit rather than a new model**: it states verbatim that it is a reliability audit of probabilistic mortality forecasts across a structural break, and that the contribution is the audit and the reusable evaluation protocol rather than a new architecture. **Measured this round**: **created 2026-08-25**, **last pushed 2026-09-08**, **one star**, primarily TeX, **licensed MIT** with a licence file naming the author and year, and **192 paths in the extracted archive**, including twenty-three test files, seven documentation files, twenty-one scripts and a full paper directory with twelve figure PDFs and complete LaTeX sources. **This entry belongs to the round theme of the downstream using the upstream as a yardstick, since it uses a pooled mortality modelling package as its numerical oracle and a pooled mortality database as its data.** **Four things are worth copying**: the preregistration carries a hash and states that it was committed before the first model was fitted to real data, with every later deviation recorded in four numbered addenda; one of the registered hypotheses is refuted by the results and that refutation is stated as the headline; seven methodology rules are described verbatim as binding rather than aspirational, including a rule that a random split must never be used because mortality panels leak trivially; and the fact that the data cannot be redistributed is stated together with a route to obtain it and a checksum manifest. **Nothing was run and no paper body was read this round.**
e.body:
**mortality-calibration-under-shift**（GitHub 仓库 `Hamid-Jahani/mortality-calibration-under-shift`）**是一份关于**概率型死亡率预测**的**可靠性审计****，**README 的标题与副标题逐字为**「**Do Mortality Prediction Intervals Survive a Pandemic? A Pre-Registered Calibration Audit of Ten Forecasting Families and Seven Uncertainty Mechanisms Across the COVID-19 Break.**」**。**本次实测**：**创建 2026-08-25、最后推送 2026-09-08**、**★1**、**主语言 TeX**；**许可 MIT**（**`LICENSE` 逐字前两行为** `MIT License`／`Copyright (c) 2026 Hamid Jahani`**）**；**tarball 枚举 192 条路径**，**其中** `tests/` **23 个文件、**`docs/` **7 份、**`scripts/` **21 个、**`paper/` **含** 12 张图 PDF ＋ `figures-manifest.json` ＋ `main.tex` ＋ `references.bib` ＋ `sections/` 10 个 `.tex` ＋ **一个 `submission/` 提交包**（**含** `COMPLIANCE.md` **与** `supp/S1-preregistration.tex` **到** `S6-infeasible.tex`**）**；**⭐ 本条目属于本轮主题**「**下游：把上游当成尺子**」**——**⭐ 它把本站已收录的 [[stmomo]] 当作**数值预言机**，**并以 [[human-mortality-db]] 为数据源**。

**可核实信息（均 README 与文件清单实测）**：**⭐⭐⭐ ① 它明说自己**不是**在提出新模型**——**逐字**：**「**A reliability audit of probabilistic mortality forecasts across a structural break. **The contribution is the audit and the reusable evaluation protocol — not a new architecture.** Model family and uncertainty mechanism are **crossed factors** (50 admissible cells, `docs/GRID.md`), so coverage failure can be attributed to the architecture or to the uncertainty machinery bolted onto it.**」**。**⭐ 本词条认为这是本轮最值得抄的一处**：**「**模型族**」与「**不确定性机制**」被做成**交叉因子**（**50 个可容许格**）**——**⭐ 即**当区间覆盖失败时，**你**能分辨**是**架构的问题**还是**后来加上去的那套不确定性机制的问题**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 预注册带哈希，且写明**早于第一次拟合****——**逐字**：**「**Status: complete. All three pre-registered regimes are swept, QA-gated (zero machine-failure rows) and analysed; the paper draft is written from them. `PREREGISTRATION.md` was committed 2026-08-25 — sha256 `bbbe3860a5446d063e186e56555afa893b07c36cf15a990d07567471affe50be` — before the first model was fitted to real data, and every deviation since is recorded in the four addenda and `docs/STATUS.md`.**」**。**⭐ 三处值得记**：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **给出 sha256**——**⭐ 即**「**我事先写下了什么**」**可被第三方校验**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **明确「**早于第一次用真实数据拟合**」**——**⭐ 因为**「**先注册**」这件事只有在**时间顺序**上成立才有意义**；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **所有偏离**记在四份 addenda 里****（**文件清单实测确有** `PREREGISTRATION-ADDENDUM-1.md` **到** `-4.md`**）**——**⭐ 即**违背预注册不是被隐藏，**而是**被登记**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 它把一条**注册假设的否定**当成头条**——**逐字**：**「**The registered one-sided H2 is refuted. The two-sided |coverage − nominal| grows from stable to shift in only 27 of 50 cells. Coverage falls in 34 of 50, but that is degradation only for arms that began below nominal: over-covering arms move toward nominal. The break sorts families by which side of nominal they started on.**」**。**⭐ 即**「**疫情这道断点**」**并没有普遍把区间变得更差**——**它按**各模型族原本偏在哪一侧**来分类**；**⭐ 本词条认为这与本站第 336 轮「**宁可拒绝也不假装**」同向**：**预注册的价值正在于**结果与预期不符时你得照写**。**⭐⭐ ④ 结论里有一条**对实务最有用****——**逐字**：**「**H5 is the practical warning. Annuity-factor intervals are far worse than rate-level ones and are already broken in quiet periods: Lee–Carter’s nominal 95% interval for ä₆₅ covers 0.253 of realisations in the stable control.**」**。**⭐ 即**名义 95% 的区间在**平静期**只覆盖约 **四分之一**——**⭐ 而**这条恰好是**年金（ä₆₅）**而非**死亡率本身**的区间**，**也就是**精算实务真正要用的那个量**。**⭐ 另两条结论逐字为**：**平静期对照下经典原生区间已只覆盖 **0.702**（Lee–Carter）、**0.682**（Poisson-LC）、**0.731**（APC/RH），**而名义为 0.95**——**⭐ 即**「**大部分失准在疫情之前就存在了**」（**逐字**「**Most miscalibration predates the pandemic.**」**）**；**以及**「**H3 holds universally — joint path coverage is below marginal in 100 of 100 (regime, cell) pairs.**」**。**⭐⭐⭐ ⑤ 七条方法学规则被逐字称为**「**binding, not aspirational**」****——**逐字七条**：**① `PREREGISTRATION.md` **在第一次拟合之前提交并带哈希**；**② **只用扩展窗口的时间切分**，**「**Never a random split — mortality panels leak trivially.**」；**③ **超参只在**内层时间切分**上调，**绝不在测试集上调**；**④ **每个模型都要输出**预测分布**，**而不是点预测**；**⑤ **评测框架在接触真实数据之前**先用**已知 Lee–Carter 数据生成过程**的**合成真值**验证过**（**⭐ 文件清单里确有** `tests/test_synthetic_calibration.py`**）**；**⑥ **Python 的 Lee–Carter 与 R 的 StMoMo 在 α、β、k 上**达到数值一致**（**逐字给出**「**β relative difference 2.4e-14**」**）**；**⑦ **每个集成成员的**随机种子**都被记录**。**⭐ 即**这七条**每一条都可以被检查**，**而不是「**我们很小心**」。**⭐⭐ ⑥ 数据不可再分发，**并且给了自取路径与校验清单****——**逐字**：**「**The `Dataset/` tree is **not committed**. HMD’s user agreement restricts redistribution: obtain the data yourself from <https://www.mortality.org/Data/ZippedDataFiles> after free registration. `data/MANIFEST.sha256` pins the exact file vintage this work uses. Verify a local copy from the repository root: `sha256sum -c data/MANIFEST.sha256`**」**。**⭐ 即**「**我不能把数据给你**」**之后紧接**「**你可以自己取，**取到之后用这个清单核对版本**」**——**⭐ 而数据版本逐字为**「**49 populations, vintage 15 Jun 2026**」**。**⭐⭐ ⑦ 研究过程被留下了可数的痕迹**——**文件清单一处可数**：`docs/` **下有** `GRID.md`、`SPLIT-SPEC.md`、`PIPELINE.md`、`NEURAL-SPEC.md`、`PRIOR-ART.md`、`DATA-PREREQS.md`、`STATUS.md`；`literature/` **下有** `INDEX.md`、`TRIAGE.md`、`GAP-ANALYSIS.md`、`GET-THESE.md`、`MISSING.md`；`scripts/` **下有 21 个**，**含** `oracle_parity.R`、`final_qa.py`、`verify_quotes.py`、`time_cells.py`、`sweep_cost.py`、`make_figures.py`、`make_tables.py`、`make_submission_zip.sh` **与** `server_*` **一组**；`src/mortcal/` **下** `models/`（**lc、cbd、rh、svar、neural、gp**）、**`uq/`**（**bootstrap、conformal、neural**）、`eval/scores.py`、`data/hmd.py`、`lifetable.py`、`splits.py`、`inference.py`、`runner.py`；**运行方式逐字为** `uv run pytest -q`（**Python 3.12 由 uv 固定**）**。**⭐ 本词条认为**这三点尤其值得抄**：**① **文献一节自带**「**还缺哪些**」**（`MISSING.md`）**与**「**要弄到这些**」**（`GET-THESE.md`**）**；**② **有一个脚本叫** `verify_quotes.py`**（**⚠️ 本次未读其内容，故不主张它核对什么**）**；**③ **投稿包与工作稿分开**（`paper/` **与** `paper/submission/`**）**。**⭐⭐ ⑧ 与池内条目的关系**：**本站 [[human-mortality-db]] 提供数据**，**[[stmomo]]、[[mortalitylaws]]、[[mortcast]]、[[cmi-mortality-projections]]、[[mortality-dynamics]]、[[mortalityforecast]]、[[affinemortality]]、[[bayesmortalityplus]] 覆盖死亡率建模方法**，**[[reproducible-actuarial-work]]、[[verified-reserving]] 覆盖可复现与验证**——**⭐ 而本条补上的是**「**预注册审查 ＋ 交叉因子网格 ＋ 把同名假设的否定写进结论**」这一形态**。

**对 RIAA**：**本条与 [[stmomo]]、[[human-mortality-db]] 应当并读**——**它给的是「**这些模型的区间到底可不可信**」这一问题上**一份带具体覆盖率数字的审计**；**⭐ 而对本词条项目最有借鉴的三点**：**① 预注册要**带哈希并写明时间顺序**；**② 结果与预期不符时**照写**，**并把偏离记在**附录**里**；**③ 数据**不能再分发时**，**给出**自取路径 ＋ 版本校验清单**。

**⚠️ 本词条如实标注**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次没有运行该项目任何一步**（**未跑** `uv run pytest`、**未跑任何 sweep、**未生成任何表或图、**未取 HMD 数据**），**故不主张**其任何覆盖率数字、**不主张** H1–H5 的结论、**也不主张**其校验门（**合成真值、**StMoMo 一致性、**生命表一致性**）真的通过**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未读论文任何正文**——**本次只读了** `README.md` **与文件清单**，**未打开** `paper/main.tex`、**10 个** `sections/*.tex`、**投稿包** `submission/`**、**也未读** `PREREGISTRATION.md` **与四份 addenda 的正文**（**⭐ 本次只看到它们**存在**与其在 README 中被引用的方式**）**。**⚠️ 本条目最需后续核实的一处**。**③ ⚠️ 未核实** `PREREGISTRATION.md` **的**实际提交时间**与其**sha256 是否与 README 所述一致**——**⭐ 本词条只转述 README 的说法**（**⭐ 且**未用 `git log` 核对该文件的历史**）**。**④ ⚠️ 未核实**「**50 个可容许格**」**与**「**100 of 100**」**这两个计数的构成**（**未读** `docs/GRID.md`**）**；**未核实** `docs/STATUS.md` **里记了哪些偏离**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核实数据来源与许可细节**：**未访问** mortality.org **或 HMD 的用户协议页**，**故**「**HMD 的用户协议限制再分发**」**这一说法**本次**只记录为**该项目自述**。**⑥ ⚠️ 未核实作者身份与所属机构**；**★1 不构成质量证据**；**⚠️ 该项目**未被任何期刊接收**这一事实**本词条不主张也不推测**（**README 只说**「**the paper draft is written from them**」**）**。**⑦ ⚠️ 许可为 MIT（`LICENSE` 存在，**本次读到前两行**）**，**未读正文**；**⭐ 并如实指出**：**数据本身**受 HMD 协议约束**，**与代码的 MIT 许可**是两件事**。**⑧ ⚠️ 创建 2026-08-25 在解冻窗口之外、推送 2026-09-08 在窗口之内**——**本次按惯例把这一处写在这里**：**本条的缺口是「**预注册审查 ＋ 模型族与不确定性机制的交叉网格 ＋ 把注册假设的否定写进结论**」这一形态此前池内没有对应物**。**⑨ ⚠️ 本条目所记为 2026-09-11 所见**；**⚠️ 并如实提示**：**本词条不主张该项目覆盖率的数字可用于任何具体定价或准备金判断**。

Model family and uncertainty mechanism are crossed factors (50 admissible cells, `docs/GRID.md`)**」**——**⭐ 即**當區間覆蓋失敗時，**你**能分辨**是**架構的問題**還是**後來加上去的不確定性機制**的問題**。**⭐⭐⭐ ② 預註冊帶雜湊，且寫明**早於第一次擬合****——**逐字**「**`PREREGISTRATION.md` was committed 2026-08-25 — sha256 `bbbe3860a5446d063e186e56555afa893b07c36cf15a990d07567471affe50be` — before the first model was fitted to real data, and every deviation since is recorded in the four addenda and `docs/STATUS.md`.**」**——**⭐ 三處值得記**：**給出 sha256**、**寫明時間順序**、**所有偏離記在四份 addenda**（**清單實測確有** `PREREGISTRATION-ADDENDUM-1.md` **到** `-4.md`**）**。**⭐⭐⭐ ③ 它把一條**註冊假設的否定**當成頭條**——**逐字**「**The registered one-sided H2 is refuted. Coverage falls in 34 of 50, but that is degradation only for arms that began below nominal: over-covering arms move toward nominal.**」**。**⭐⭐ ④ 結論裡有一條**對實務最有用****——**逐字**「**Annuity-factor intervals are far worse than rate-level ones and are already broken in quiet periods: Lee–Carter’s nominal 95% interval for ä₆₅ covers 0.253 of realisations in the stable control.**」**——**⭐ 即**名義 95% 的區間在**平靜期**只覆蓋約**四分之一**，**而這條恰好是**年金**而非死亡率本身的區間**。**⭐⭐⭐ ⑤ 七條方法學規則逐字被稱為**「**binding, not aspirational**」**（**含**「**Never a random split — mortality panels leak trivially.**」**、**「**每個模型都要輸出預測分布**」**、**「**評測框架先用合成真值驗證**」**、**「**Python Lee–Carter 與 R StMoMo 在 α、β、k 上數值一致（β relative difference 2.4e-14）**」**、**「**每個集成成員的種子都記錄**」**）**。**⭐⭐ ⑥ 資料不可再分發，**並給出自取路徑與校驗清單****——**逐字**「**HMD’s user agreement restricts redistribution: obtain the data yourself after free registration. `data/MANIFEST.sha256` pins the exact file vintage**」**（**資料版本逐字為**「**49 populations, vintage 15 Jun 2026**」**）**。**⭐⭐ ⑦ 過程留痕可數**：`docs/` 7 份、`literature/` **5 份（含** `MISSING.md` **與** `GET-THESE.md`**）**、`scripts/` 21 個（**含** `oracle_parity.R`、`verify_quotes.py`、`final_qa.py`**）**、`src/mortcal/` **含** models（lc／cbd／rh／svar／neural／gp**）與** uq（bootstrap／conformal／neural**）**；**執行逐字為** `uv run pytest -q`**。

**對 RIAA**：**本條與 [[stmomo]]、[[human-mortality-db]] 應當並讀**——**⭐ 三點最值得借鑑**：**① 預註冊要**帶雜湊並寫明時間順序**；② 結果與預期不符時**照寫**，**並把偏離記在附錄**；③ 資料不能再分發時，**給出自取路徑＋版本校驗清單**。

**⚠️ 本詞條如實標註**：**① ⚠️⚠️⚠️ 本次沒有運行該專案任何一步**，**故不主張**其任何覆蓋率數字、**不主張** H1–H5 的結論、**也不主張**其校驗門真的通過**。**② ⚠️⚠️ 未讀論文任何正文**——**只讀** `README.md` **與文件清單**，**未打開** `paper/main.tex`、`sections/*.tex`、投稿包、**也未讀** `PREREGISTRATION.md` **與四份 addenda 的正文**。**⚠️ 本條目最需後續核實的一處**。**③ ⚠️ 未核實** `PREREGISTRATION.md` **的實際提交時間與其 sha256 是否與 README 所述一致**（**未用** `git log` **核對**）**。**④ ⚠️ 未核實**「**50 個可容許格**」**與**「**100 of 100**」**這兩個計數的構成**。**⑤ ⚠️ 未核實 HMD 用戶協議細節**（**未訪問** mortality.org**）**，**該說法只記為**專案自述**。**⑥ ⚠️ 未核實作者身份與機構**；**★1 不構成品質證據**。**⑦ ⚠️ 許可為 MIT，未讀正文**；**⭐ 資料本身受 HMD 協議約束，**與代碼許可**是兩件事**。**⑧ ⚠️ 建立 2026-08-25 在解凍窗口之外、推送 2026-09-08 在窗口之內**——**本條的缺口是「預註冊審查＋交叉網格＋把註冊假設的否定寫進結論」這一形態此前池內沒有對應物**。**⑨ ⚠️ 本條目所記為 2026-09-11 所見**；**⚠️ 不主張其覆蓋率數字可用於任何具體定價或準備金判斷**。

e.body_en:
The repository mortality-calibration-under-shift **is a reliability audit of probabilistic mortality forecasts**, titled and subtitled as asking whether mortality prediction intervals survive a pandemic and describing itself as a pre-registered calibration audit of ten forecasting families and seven uncertainty mechanisms across a pandemic break. **Measured this round**: **created 2026-08-25**, **last pushed 2026-09-08**, **one star**, primarily TeX, **licensed MIT** with a licence file naming the author and year, and **192 paths in the extracted archive**, including twenty-three test files, seven documentation files, twenty-one scripts, and a paper directory holding twelve figure PDFs with a figures manifest, a main LaTeX file, a bibliography, ten section files and a full submission package with a compliance note and six supplementary files. **This entry belongs to the round theme of the downstream using the upstream as a yardstick, because it uses a pooled mortality modelling package as its numerical oracle and a pooled mortality database as its data.**

**Verified information, all measured from the README and the file listing**: **first, it states that it is not proposing a new model**: verbatim, it is a reliability audit of probabilistic mortality forecasts across a structural break, and the contribution is the audit and the reusable evaluation protocol rather than a new architecture; model family and uncertainty mechanism are crossed factors across fifty admissible cells, so a coverage failure can be attributed to the architecture or to the uncertainty machinery bolted onto it. **When interval coverage fails, you can therefore tell whether the architecture or the uncertainty layer added on top is responsible, which this entry considers the most copyable idea of the round.** **Second, the preregistration carries a hash and states that it predates the first fit**: verbatim, the preregistration file was committed on a stated date with a full SHA-256 hash before the first model was fitted to real data, and every deviation since is recorded in four addenda and a status file. **The hash means a third party can check what was written in advance, the phrase before the first fit makes the ordering explicit, and the fact that all deviations are logged in four numbered addenda means departing from the preregistration is registered rather than hidden.** **Third, it makes the refutation of one of its own registered hypotheses a headline**: verbatim, the registered one-sided hypothesis is refuted, the two-sided distance between coverage and nominal grows from stable to shift in only twenty-seven of fifty cells, coverage falls in thirty-four of fifty, but that counts as degradation only for arms that began below nominal, since over-covering arms move toward nominal, and the break sorts families by which side of nominal they started on. **The pandemic break did not uniformly make intervals worse; it reclassified families according to the side of nominal they started on, and the value of preregistration is exactly that an unexpected result still has to be written down.** **Fourth, one finding is the practical warning**: annuity-factor intervals are far worse than rate-level ones and are already broken in quiet periods, with a nominal ninety-five percent interval for an annuity factor covering only about a quarter of realisations in the stable control. **The interval that actuarial practice actually needs is the annuity one rather than the mortality rate one, and it is the worse of the two.** Two further findings are stated verbatim: most miscalibration predates the pandemic, with classical native intervals in the quiet stable control covering about seventy, sixty-eight and seventy-three percent against a nominal ninety-five; and joint path coverage is below marginal coverage in one hundred of one hundred regime and cell pairs. **Fifth, seven methodology rules are described verbatim as binding rather than aspirational**: the preregistration is committed and hash-stamped before the first fit; expanding-origin temporal splits only are used, never a random split, because mortality panels leak trivially; hyperparameters tune on an inner time split and never on the test set; every model emits a predictive distribution rather than a point forecast; the evaluation harness is validated against synthetic truth from a known data-generating process before it touches real data, which the file listing corroborates with a synthetic calibration test; the Python implementation matches the R oracle to numerical tolerance on all three parameters, with a reported relative difference of about two in ten to the fourteenth; and seeds are recorded per ensemble member. **Every one of those rules is checkable rather than being a claim of care.** **Sixth, the data cannot be redistributed and the repository says so while providing a route and a checksum manifest**: the dataset tree is not committed, the database user agreement restricts redistribution, readers are told to obtain the data themselves after free registration, a manifest pins the exact file vintage, and verification is a checksum command. **Refusing to hand over the data is immediately followed by how to get it yourself and how to confirm you got the same version**, with the vintage stated as forty-nine populations from a June 2026 release. **Seventh, the research process leaves countable traces**: seven documentation files including grid, split specification, pipeline, neural specification, prior art, data prerequisites and status; five literature files including an index, a triage, a gap analysis, a to-get list and a list of what is missing; twenty-one scripts including an oracle parity script in R, a final quality gate, a quote verification script, a cell timing script, a sweep cost script and figure and table builders; and a source package with data, model, uncertainty, evaluation, life table, split and inference modules covering six model families and three uncertainty mechanisms, run through a pinned Python environment. **Three of those are especially worth copying: the literature section carries its own list of what is still missing and what to obtain; there is a script whose name suggests verifying quotes; and the submission package is kept separate from the working draft.** **Eighth, relative to existing entries**: pooled entries supply the mortality database and the modelling methods, and pooled entries cover reproducibility and verification, while this entry supplies pre-registered auditing, a crossed-factor grid and the practice of putting the refutation of a registered hypothesis into the conclusions.

**For RIAA**: **this entry reads alongside [[stmomo]] and [[human-mortality-db]]**, because **it is an audit with concrete coverage numbers for the question of whether these model intervals can be trusted at all**, and because **three practices transfer directly: preregister with a hash and state the ordering in time, write the result down even when it contradicts the expectation and log deviations in an appendix, and when data cannot be redistributed give a route to obtain it plus a version checksum**.

**Marked honestly by this entry**: **first, no step of the project was run** — no test suite, no sweep, no table or figure generation and no data retrieval — **so none of its coverage numbers is claimed, none of the five hypotheses is claimed to be settled, and none of its validation gates is claimed to pass**. **Second, no paper body was read**: only the README and the file listing were read, and neither the main LaTeX file, the ten section files, the submission package, nor the preregistration file and its four addenda were opened; **this is the item most in need of later verification**. **Third, the actual commit date of the preregistration file and whether its hash matches the README statement were not verified**, since its history was not inspected; **this entry relays the README statement only**. **Fourth, the composition of the fifty admissible cells and of the one-hundred-of-one-hundred count was not verified**, nor was what deviations the status file records. **Fifth, the database user agreement was not consulted**, so the claim that redistribution is restricted is recorded as the project own statement. **Sixth, the author identity and affiliation were not verified, and one star is not evidence of quality; this entry neither claims nor speculates about whether the paper has been accepted anywhere**, the README saying only that the draft is written from the results. **Seventh, the licence is MIT and its text was not read, and this entry states plainly that the data itself is governed by a separate agreement, which is a different matter from the code licence. Eighth, the creation date of 2026-08-25 is outside the thaw window while the push of 2026-09-08 is inside it**, and following the project convention of naming the gap, **the gap here is that a pre-registered audit with a crossed grid of model families and uncertainty mechanisms, and a registered hypothesis refuted in its own conclusions, had no counterpart in the pool. Ninth, this entry records what was visible on 2026-09-11, and states plainly that none of its coverage figures should be used for any specific pricing or reserving judgement.**
